writeup: Astronomers have identified a new eclipsing binary star system called TIC 294976780, never before cataloged in any major variable-star database. The two stars orbit each other in just 0.9586 days, and when the primary star passes in front of its companion, the system dims by 4.90 percent. A secondary eclipse was not detected. The discovery was confirmed through multiple independent methods: a strong signal-to-noise detection of 133.1 using automated analysis, followed by pixel-level verification showing a peak signal-to-noise of 17.0 with the predicted offset of 2.0 arcseconds from the target location. The system passed all data quality checks, making this a clean, genuine addition to known binary star systems.
